newsitem.title: USA: U.S. opposes appointment of Cambodian co-premier.
newsitem.headline: U.S. opposes appointment of Cambodian co-premier.

text.p: The United States said on Wednesday it was "very concerned" by a decision to make Cambodian Foreign Minister Ung Huot the country's co-prime minister and did not recognise him in that position.
A dissident faction of ousted First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party said on Wednesday it would nominate Ung Huot as the prince's replacement.

Second Prime Minister Hun Sen overthrew Ranariddh on July 6 but said he wanted the coalition between his Cambodian People's Party and Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC to remain in place and for the royalist party to choose a new first prime minister.

"We are very concerned about the decision this morning to make the Cambodian foreign minister co-prime minister with Hun Sen," said State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns. "We see no evidence whatsoever that FUNCINPEC has met ... and has elected on a free basis ... a successor to Prince Ranariddh."

"We urge the authorities in Phnom Penh to refrain from announcing a new first prime minister until Prince Ranariddh's political party has an opportunity to make a reasoned decision on this matter, free of coercion, free of intimidation," Burns told a news briefing.

Burns said the United States had dealt "very cooperatively" with Ung Huot as foreign minister in the past, "but we don't recognise him as first prime minister, we recognise Prince Ranariddh as first prime minister."
